deadline.value: Applications for financial aid are due January 15, earlier than the Graduate School's April 15 deadline.
deadline.quote: Application for admission with financial aid: Jan. 15.

gre_subject.value: The Subject (Physics) GRE is not required but is strongly recommended.
gre_subject.quote: but you are strongly recommended to take it

supervisor.value: Applications are reviewed by the admissions committee, and the department page sets no advisor agreement before admission.
supervisor.quote: The admissions committee begins reviewing applications shortly after Jan.1.

funding.value: In general, PhD students receive a fellowship, teaching assistantship or research assistantship that covers tuition and a stipend.
funding.quote: In general, all students in the Ph.D. program are supported with a fellowship, teaching assistantship or research assistantship.

entry_route.value: The department pages do not say whether a master's degree is needed.

fee_waiver.value: The Graduate School offers no fee waiver, but the department has a few competitive scholarships that pay application fees.
fee_waiver.quote: the Department of Physics and Astronomy has scholarships which can be used to pay the application fees of a small number of applicants

gre_general.value: The GRE is not required; applicants may self-report scores.
gre_general.quote: No. However, if you have taken the GRE, you may self-report the scores.

notes: Department rules are stated on its application page and FAQ. The FAQ's TOEFL and IELTS paragraph quotes the Graduate School's older 79 / 6.5 text, so no program-level English override is set. The department page says the Graduate School does not offer application fee waivers, which conflicts with the Graduate School military-veteran waiver; the department's own scholarship rule is used.
name: Physics (PhD)
